name: Adoption timeline

subjectOf.text: Private fund adoption of blockchain began in 2012, coinciding with the broader public debate over blockchain solutions, and took the form of managers setting up separate new fund entities that used the technology.
subjectOf.abstract: In 2012, coinciding with the more public debate of blockchain based solutions, private investment fund managers started to get involved in the technology by setting up separate and new fund entities that utilized the technology in various forms.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Innovation for Private Investment Funds (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998033
scope_conditions: based on the study's time series of fund inception versus blockchain use inception dates

subjectOf.text: Blockchain adoption by private investment funds followed a staged path: minimal use from 2000 to 2012, then experimentation through separate new fund entities beginning in 2012, and from 2015 the creation of blockchain substructures inside existing funds.
subjectOf.abstract: They began to experiment with the technology by setting up separate and new fund entities that utilized the technology in various forms. In 2015, however, existing funds also started to create substructures that utilized blockchain technology.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Financial Technology and Hedge Funds (2019). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3409548

subjectOf.text: Development of blockchain based processes will take several years if not decades, so the most likely outcome is that legacy and blockchain based issuance, trading, and settlement systems coexist side by side for the foreseeable future.
subjectOf.abstract: will take several years if not decades, and so the most likely circumstance is that legacy and blockchain-based securities issuance, trading, settlement, and related systems and processes will have to co-exist side-by-side for the foreseeable future.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110
scope_conditions: transition period for securities market infrastructure

subjectOf.text: Because Impact 3.0 growth depends on donor realization, willingness to run parallel tracks, standardization, critical mass of listings, funding sources and credential tracking, only a smaller subset of the philanthropy market will be attracted to impact certificate markets, and full establishment may take five to ten years.
subjectOf.abstract: Given these dependencies, a smaller subset of the philanthropy market will be attracted to impact certificate markets. It may take five to ten years for the impact certificate marketplace to fully establish itself and scale in impact donor circles.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Impact Investing Innovation - From Impact 1.0 to 3.0 (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4685567
scope_conditions: multiple listed dependencies must be satisfied
